text:
sasha: Heads up — found a repro where Authorization header gets dropped on 307 redirect in the Android sample app (emulator API 30). Logs and minimal repro below.

ben: Ugh, annoying. Can you paste the client config?

sasha: Minimal OkHttp/Retrofit setup: interceptor adds Authorization then we call endpoint that returns 307 -> Location to same host. After redirect the Authorization header is missing from the follow-up request. Repro snippet: 
```kotlin
val client = OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .followRedirects(true)
  .addInterceptor { chain ->
    val req = chain.request().newBuilder()
      .addHeader("Authorization", "Bearer ${'$'}{Auth.token}")
      .build()
    chain.proceed(req)
  }
  .build()
```
Response log (trimmed):
```
-> GET /protected/resource HTTP/1.1
Host: example.internal
Authorization: Bearer abc123
<- 307 Temporary Redirect Location: /new/resource
-> GET /new/resource HTTP/1.1
Host: example.internal
# Authorization header MISSING here
```

clara: That matches OkHttp behavior: application interceptors are invoked only once for the original call; redirected network-level requests can bypass them, so headers added there won't automatically be present for follow-up network requests. Network interceptors see each network request.

ben: Workarounds: either add header in a network interceptor, or set followRedirects(false) and handle Location yourself (rebuild request + copy headers). Network interceptor example: 
```kotlin
.addNetworkInterceptor { chain ->
  val token = tokenProvider.getTokenSync() // must be sync/blocking here
  val req = chain.request().newBuilder()
    .header("Authorization", "Bearer ${'$'}token")
    .build()
  chain.proceed(req)
}
```

sasha: Confirmed: switching to addNetworkInterceptor fixed it in the emulator. Caveat: our token provider is suspend/refreshing and can't be called from network interceptor without blocking. I hacked a sync token cache for the sampleapp which made it work.

clara: Another pattern: use an Authenticator for 401/407 flows so you refresh tokens only on challenge, but that doesn't help redirects. Also be careful to NOT forward Authorization to a different host on redirects — check host == originalHost before copying header.

ben: Good security note. Also saw Android-specific quirk: when followRedirects is true and a streaming response is interrupted by a redirect, OkHttp can close the socket and trigger SocketTimeoutException if timeouts are tight. Increasing read timeout or handling redirect manually avoids that in our CI emulator runs.

sasha: Filed quick ticket with steps and logs, attaching sampleapp branch. CI repro: emulator-api-30 group fails 1/3 runs.

ci-bot: deploy-bot: CI failure detected for sampleapp-e2e (emulator-api-30). Created issue RNW-2341.

ben: I'll put together a small reproducible sample and open a PR in dev-examples. Plan: show three options — networkInterceptor, manual redirect handler (followRedirects=false), and Authenticator + docs about host check + blocking token caveat.

sasha: :thumbsup: please include test matrix (Android 9/10/11/12/13) and a note about not using network interceptor if token refresh is async (prefer a short-lived sync cache or manual redirect handling).

clara: Also add a short blurb in the SDK FAQ: "Why did my Authorization header disappear after a redirect?" with link to OkHttp interceptor docs and the security host-check example.

sasha: Great, thanks all. I'll link the sampleapp PR in the ticket when ready.
